1. Policy: Each fisher may harvest no more than 5% of the lake’s current biomass per trip, and the lake must maintain a communal reserve of at least 25% of its total biomass at all times.
   In practice: On each fishing trip, the fisher records the weight taken and reports it to the community ledger. After each round, the community council updates the lake’s total biomass, calculates the required reserve (25% of the current total), and ensures no fisher’s haul exceeded 5% of the lake before the haul. If a fisher exceeds the 5% limit or the reserve drops below 25%, the fisher must return the excess catch to the lake and pay a fine of 1kg for each kg over the limit. The council may suspend the fisher’s right to fish for one round if the violation persists. All data is stored in a shared ledger visible to everyone.

2. Policy: Each fisher may take no more than 3 kg per trip, 15 kg per month, and the community must keep a reserve equal to 25 % of the lake’s current biomass; any catch beyond these limits is immediately released.
   In practice: On the first day of each month, every fisher reports their cumulative monthly catch to the community ledger and records any released catch. The lake’s current biomass is measured by the designated lake biologist and used to calculate the 25 % reserve threshold. If a fisher exceeds the 3 kg per‑trip limit, they must release the excess immediately and note it in the ledger. If a fisher exceeds the 15 kg per‑month limit, they are barred from fishing for one week, and the biologist will re‑evaluate the lake’s biomass after the ban before lifting the restriction. All violations are recorded and discussed at the monthly community meeting, and repeated non‑compliance results in a permanent ban until the fisher has a documented record of meeting the limits for three consecutive months.

3. Policy: No fisher may harvest more than 4% of the lake’s current biomass in any 7‑day cycle, must observe a 3‑day rest between sessions, and must log all catch; 10% of each fisher’s catch is deposited into a community reserve for stocking.
   In practice: Each fisher records catch on a shared ledger immediately after the session. The ledger is reviewed weekly by a rotating treasurer. After recording, 10% of the weight is automatically deducted and added to the reserve pool, the rest goes home. A fisher must not fish again until 3 calendar days after the last session. If a fisher exceeds the 4% limit or skips the 10% deposit, the excess or missing weight is forfeited to the reserve. The reserve is used to purchase and release hatchery stock every 6 months to maintain population size.

4. Policy: Each fisher may catch up to 5 kg per trip, keep at least 1 kg for personal sustenance, deposit the remainder into a communal reserve capped at 150 kg; if the lake stock falls below 40 kg, the catch limit drops to 3 kg per fisher.
   In practice: On each trip a fisher logs total catch and personal keep; the community ledger updates the reserve after deposits; the reserve level is checked before each trip and if the cap would be exceeded, the fisher must reduce catch accordingly. If the lake stock drops below 40 kg, the community announces the reduced limit in the next gathering. Anyone who fails to keep the minimum personal share or overdraws the reserve must forfeit the excess catch and may be temporarily banned from fishing until they repay by returning surplus to the reserve.

5. Policy: Each fisher may harvest no more than 10% of the lake’s measured biomass per 6‑month cycle, get 1 kg subsistence, and share the rest proportionally to the previous two cycles’ catch. Any excess must be returned to the lake.
   In practice: Every 6 months the community measures the lake’s biomass, announces the 10% quota. Each fisher records catch on a shared log, returns any surplus to a communal holding area that is returned to the lake. Quarterly meetings review biomass and adjust quotas. A fisher who fails to return surplus must pay a penalty of 20% of the excess, and the community may restrict that fisher’s next quota until compliance.

6. Policy: Solo may take up to 12 % of the lake’s current stock per trip; every other fisher may take up to 8 % per trip.
   In practice: Before each trip, the current lake stock is recorded by a communal tally. Each fisher weighs his catch, records it, and the total is compared to the allowed limit. If a fisher exceeds his limit, the excess must be returned to the lake or paid as a penalty fee; repeated violations trigger a temporary fishing ban. Weekly, the lake stock is re‑measured; if it falls below 60 kg, all limits drop to 5 % for one month. All data is logged in a shared ledger that the community can audit.

7. Policy: Each fisher may harvest up to 12 kg per trip, with 5 % of the catch deposited into a communal reserve that must always hold at least 20 kg in the lake.
   In practice: On each fishing day, a fisher records the total catch on a shared ledger. They then transfer 5 % of that catch to a communal tank; if the tank falls below 20 kg after a day’s haul, the extra 5 % from that fisher’s catch that day is added to make up the shortfall. If a fisher fails to deposit the required amount, they lose the right to fish for the next two days and must pay a small fee to the community fund.

8. Policy: Each fisherman may take a maximum of 12 kg per trip, the community’s total daily catch may not exceed 90 kg, and the lake must retain at least 50 kg of fish at all times.
   In practice: On each fishing day every fisher submits a log of their catch to the community leader who verifies the total against the 90 kg cap. The lake’s stock is measured by a quarterly inventory; if the remaining fish falls below 50 kg, fishing is suspended until the stock recovers. Anyone caught exceeding the 12 kg individual limit must return the excess catch and pay a community fee equal to 10 % of the over‑catch, and violations are reviewed by a council that can impose temporary bans.

9. Policy: No fisher may take more than 4 kg per trip, and the lake’s stock must never fall below 35 kg; if it dips, all fishing stops until the stock recovers to 35 kg.
   In practice: Before each trip, fishers write down the expected catch and sign a shared log. After returning, they report the actual catch; if anyone exceeds 4 kg or the lake falls below 35 kg, the community meets immediately to vote on a 1‑round suspension for that fisher and forfeits the excess catch. If the lake is at or above 35 kg, fishing continues normally.

10. Policy: Each fisher may take up to 10% of the lake’s current stock per trip, capped at 10 kg, and the lake must retain at least 30% of its stock before the next fishing event.
   In practice: At the start of each trip, a community monitor records the lake’s stock. Each fisher submits a catch ticket stating kg taken. The sum of all tickets must not exceed 70% of the recorded stock; no individual ticket may exceed the 10%/10 kg cap. If a fisher exceeds limits, their ticket is voided, they forfeit the catch, and a community penalty (e.g., a small fee or a skipped next trip) is imposed. Compliance is checked each round; non‑compliance leads to loss of fishing rights until the next cycle.
